title: Effectiveness of Spelling Interventions for Learners with Dyslexia: A Meta-Analysis and Systematic Review
population: 34 controlled trials; dyslexia/spelling deficits; children, adolescents and adults
finding: Phonics, spelling conventions and morphology improved spelling; memorisation-only advantage not confirmed
limitations: Different orthographies and varied interventions; no single best game mechanism

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of implementation and effectiveness of spelling instruction and intervention
finding: Group g≈0.319; modest improvement over active alternatives; transfer limited
limitations: Heterogeneous studies, limited tests of personalisation

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Spelling Interventions for Students With or At-Risk for Learning Disabilities
population: 59 studies; 2,229 students K–9 with/at risk of LD
finding: Group spelling g=0.33, word reading g=0.25; whole-word and multilinguistic subgroups positive
limitations: Subgroup comparisons do not isolate best method; generalisation unclear

title: Structured Literacy: Effective Instruction for Students with Dyslexia and Related Reading Difficulties
population: Students with dyslexia and related reading difficulties
finding: Explicit, systematic, cumulative instruction in phonology, orthography and morphology
limitations: Guidance synthesis, not an experimental comparison of a specific app

title: Spelling
finding: Connect sounds, graphemes, conventions and meaning; teach irregular elements explicitly
limitations: Some recommendations are informed practice rather than directly causal app studies

title: National curriculum in England: English programmes of study
finding: Sound-to-grapheme spelling; common exceptions, morphology, etymology; word-specific rehearsal
limitations: Policy and curriculum source; not controlled efficacy study

title: Spelling
finding: Syllables, highlight tricky elements, prefixes/suffixes, word building and mnemonics
limitations: Not evidence that any individual mnemonic or modality is superior

title: The Effects of Morphological Instruction on Literacy Outcomes for Children in English-Speaking Countries
finding: Strong effects on taught spellings (SMC/D≈0.85), weaker and uncertain transfer
limitations: Heterogeneity and imprecision; untrained-word evidence lower certainty

title: Retrieval practice benefits for spelling performance in fifth-grade children
finding: Four-day recall better after retrieval than copying when corrective feedback present
limitations: Population not exclusively dyslexic; spoken/written language transfer to English uncertain

title: Digital game-based spelling intervention for children with spelling deficits: A randomized controlled trial
population: 65 German-speaking second and third graders with spelling disorder
finding: Integrated digital training improved spelling and precursor skills; intervention-specific transfer
limitations: Small sample; German orthography; does not validate SpellQuest mechanics

title: Learning styles
finding: No convincing basis for assigning learners to fixed visual/auditory/kinaesthetic styles
limitations: Absence of evidence for learning-styles approach is not evidence against accessible modality choices

title: Current State of the Evidence: Orton-Gillingham Reading Interventions
population: K–12 at risk of word-level reading disabilities
finding: No significant differences on measured reading outcomes versus comparisons
limitations: Reading rather than specific spelling, variable study quality and methods

title: Phonics
finding: Explicit phoneme–grapheme teaching and segmentation for spelling
limitations: Main impact estimates are reading-based; cannot transfer numeric effects to spelling

author_or_body: Why Children With Dyslexia Struggle With Writing and How to Help Them
title: Why Children With Dyslexia Struggle With Writing and How to Help Them
finding: Highlights multicomponent phonics, sound-letter, morphological and orthographic analysis
limitations: Mixed studies; outcomes and comparison vary

author_or_body: SEND Plan / Education Authority Northern Ireland
title: Spelling
finding: Integrated phonological, orthographic, morphological, semantic and etymological knowledge
limitations: Practical guidance, not standalone controlled trial

title: How should spelling be taught?
finding: Assessment-led phonemic awareness, graphemes, morphology, patterns and systematic cumulative instruction
limitations: Teaching guidance, not a single experimental evaluation

title: Curriculum research review series: English
finding: Teach phoneme segmentation alongside written grapheme mapping
limitations: Reading-oriented review with spelling-relevant components

title: Spelling Interventions for Elementary and Secondary Students with Learning Disabilities: A Systematic Review
population: Elementary and secondary students with LD; 39 studies
finding: Multiple intervention practices; reports variance by age and setting
limitations: Methods and study outcomes varied; no optimal digital interface established

title: Retrieval practice benefits for spelling performance in fifth-grade children
finding: Retrieval with immediate corrective feedback improved 4-day spelling retention relative to copying in one experiment
limitations: Not specific to dyslexia or letter tile and recognition conditions

title: Retrieval practice with short-answer multiple-choice and hybrid tests
finding: Multiple-choice and short-answer both supported learning with nuances depending on retrieval success
limitations: Not spelling outcomes or dyslexic learners

author_or_body: Study of orthographic learning in children with spelling and reading deficits
title: Orthographic learning in children with isolated and combined reading and spelling deficits
population: Fourth-grade children with differentiated literacy problems
finding: Some children with spelling difficulties showed intact initial learning but weaker delayed exact-spelling recall
limitations: Observational design and not an interface comparison

author_or_body: Study of testing with feedback in spelling
title: Does testing with feedback improve adult spelling skills relative to copying and reading
finding: Test-with-feedback compared with copying and reading and reported mixed advantage by outcome
limitations: Not children with dyslexia or letter tile interface

title: Enhancing intermediate dyslexic learners literacy skills: a Free State community project
population: 36 Afrikaans-speaking dyslexic intermediate learners (18 intervention; 18 comparison)
finding: Reported better word recognition and spelling following nine-month Davis-based intervention
limitations: Small specialised group; multi-component intervention; limited replication; attribution to any one activity not possible

title: The Evidence Base of Davis Methods
population: Varied program evaluations and case studies
finding: Lists positive results including provider data and several comparative reports
limitations: Developer-affiliated synthesis; substantial variation in study quality; cannot infer general superiority

title: Behavioural Interventions to Remediate Learning Disorders
population: Studies evaluating Davis approaches and other learning-disorder interventions
finding: Questions empirical basis of disorientation mechanism and generalization of outcomes
limitations: Date and review methodology require independent verification; not a standalone controlled outcome study

title: The Davis Programmes
finding: Documents principles of concept/meaning mastery and experiential learning
limitations: Not independent evidence of superior spelling outcomes
